question.text: Which of the following is an emotional or psychological aspect of retirement that should be addressed in retirement planning?

answer.text: Finding interests and activities to occupy spare time in retirement
Selecting the right investment products for the distribution stage

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series XVII Retirement Adviser workbook (page 29), retirement has emotional and psychological aspects that include filling spare time, pursuing interests/hobbies, maintaining a separate social structure outside work, and managing health-related psychological effects. The page 30 sample question specifically keys "finding interests to occupy time" as a non-financial concern. The Trap: Options A, C, and D are financial planning tasks (corpus calculation, product selection, income replacement ratio); the question asks for an emotional/psychological aspect, which only option B addresses. Note: A Retirement Adviser should help clients prepare for the non-financial side of retirement - hobbies, social structures, and health-linked psychological wellbeing - alongside the corpus and income plan.
